rationale: The maturity journey explicitly builds on data flow mapping as its foundation: 'you cannot segment without understanding flows.'
The sequential maturity framework requires macro segmentation as the second phase after data flow mapping.
Micro segmentation is the third phase in the integrated maturity progression.
'You cannot micro-segment effectively without macro segmentation as a foundation.' Micro segmentation builds on macro.
'You can't segment what you don't understand' — data flow mapping is the prerequisite that enables effective macro segmentation.
Macro segmentation between business functions is the primary mechanism for preventing lateral movement, which is the pillar's core purpose.
Micro segmentation limits the blast radius when lateral movement occurs, directly serving the pillar's raison d'être.
East-west segmentation is the hardest lateral movement problem — controlling traffic within the same VLAN/subnet is what most distinguishes ZT from perimeter security.
Enforcement at every OSI layer — especially Layer 2 with SGTs — is how east-west segmentation within the same VLAN becomes technically feasible.
The historical narrative that perimeter security was an accident of NAT/IP isolation, not a designed property, explains and reinforces why it is now obsolete.
Perimeter failure — attackers who breach the perimeter face no further barriers — is exactly why lateral movement prevention becomes the central ZT concern.
VPNs are a perimeter technology; the obsolescence of perimeter-based security directly undermines VPNs as a viable access model.
The five fatal VPN flaws provide the architectural argument for why VPN removal is a necessary consequence of ZT principles.
ZT encrypted overlays replacing dedicated WAN links supports the broader argument that VPN-based connectivity is obsolete.
Cloud-hosted PE/PA is the practical alternative to VPN hairpinning, demonstrating how ZT network transformation replaces VPNs for remote access.
Eliminating cipher suite negotiation in favor of fixed strong suites is a concrete practice that advances the cryptographic agility maturity dimension.
Assigning mTLS to client/server and IPsec to server/server demonstrates layered encryption at different OSI levels, supporting the multi-layer enforcement principle.
The CISA maturity model independently confirms that micro-segmentation with dynamic JIT connectivity is the optimal end-state, supporting the NSA's blast-radius claim.
SPA mitigates the endpoint enumeration tradeoff by hiding services until a valid cryptographically-signed packet is received, partially addressing ZT's privacy gap.
Widespread traffic encryption creates the challenge that forces IDPS to adapt — network-based IDPS is challenged by encrypted ZT tunnels, shifting advantage to host-based IDPS.
Micro segmentation extends macro segmentation by adding granular, service-specific isolation within business function segments.
East-west segmentation extends micro segmentation to its most granular level — controlling traffic between adjacent devices in the same VLAN, which is the hardest case.
The local TLS daemon architecture extends the role-separation strategy by decoupling TLS from application libraries, enabling centralized crypto policy management.
The CISA maturity model extends the NSA macro segmentation concept by specifying fully distributed ingress/egress micro-perimeters and dynamic JIT connectivity as the advanced end-state.
Dynamic traffic management extends static micro-perimeter segmentation by adding continuously evolving rules that reprioritize applications based on mission criticality and risk.

One claim positions NAC (Cisco ISE) as the single source of truth for ZT access decisions; the other declares 802.1x-based NAC fundamentally incompatible with ZT's universal scope due to local-only, coarse-grained, and static limitations.
